reviewed_finding: The node is a DEFINITION whose bottleneck says Lean for Theorems 1 and 2 was not looked for. The local source ds_qm062_u1_selector_layers_and_ring_iso is a fixed 2 x 2 integer instance (J, S, K, Z1, Z2 and one product), ds_qm062_and_l1_u1_selector_frob_exclusions_and_gaussian_ring_injectivity is general in four integers but only for 1 x 1 Gaussian integers, and the paper anchor l1_observer_h1_h5_cochain_flatness_and_wdp_window_mass_realification is an excluded aggregate (its only structural conjunct is the trivial iff (b = -c and a = d) <-> (b + c = 0 and a - d = 0)). The theorems are therefore proved afresh for general finite index types in Lean (Theorem 1 pieces and Theorem 2), the trace qualification (A = 1 + i) is a kernel instance, and J is shown to be a declaration: a different square root of -I exists and carves out a different commutant.

claim_boundary.supports: For every finite index types m, n, k and every commutative ring (kernel-checked, Matrix.fromBlocks), on the declared PAIR model of a complex matrix A = (P, Q) with the hand-written product (PS - QT, PT + QS): R is additive, ring-linear, multiplicative on composable matrices, sends the identity to the identity and is injective; J^2 = -1; J_m R(A) = R(A) J_n for rectangular A; R(iA) = J_m R(A); R(A*) = R(A)^T so A is Hermitian iff R(A) is symmetric; Tr R(A) = 2 Tr P, i.e. twice the REAL part of the complex trace (the instance A = 1 + i has complex trace 1 + i and real trace 2); Theorem 2: a matrix indexed by (m + m) x (n + n) is R(A) for exactly one A iff J_m M = M J_n; conjugating J by an invertible P transports the commutant, and an explicit unimodular instance shows [[1,-1],[2,-1]] is a second integer square root of -I that does not commute with J (kernel instance). Native (exact tables, not kernel theorems): 9 product cases up to 3 x 3 (square and rectangular, incl. A = 0, A = I, A = iI, a Hermitian A) with R(AB), R(A*) and the INTERLEAVED coordinate order (re_1, im_1, re_2, ...) which in general gives a different matrix from the block one (the two can coincide, e.g. for A = 0 or A = I); each product record states whether the interleaved matrix commutes with the block J_n, and no universal statement is made; 13 real matrices tested for membership in the image (positive cases, diag(1,0,0,0), diag(-1,1,1,1), diag(1,-1) and diag(I,-I) which anticommute with J, an odd-dimensional matrix, rectangular cases, a symmetric non-image matrix); 9 small matrices (8 Hermitian, 1 non-Hermitian refused) on which complex positive semidefiniteness and positive semidefiniteness of the real symmetric R(A) agree (instances of preservation and reflection, found by principal minors and by elimination; NOT a kernel theorem); the J-structure flags of 8 integer 2 x 2 matrices; and a brute-force census of the integer square roots of -I in the boxes B = 1, 2, 3, 5, 7: 26 solutions in the box [-5,5], of which only +-J commute with J. The census is a bounded enumeration, not a theorem; "only +-J commute with J" is shown by the census in those boxes only (the commutant of J in M_2(Z) is {aI + bJ}, but that argument is not in the module).
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Any selection of J or of the complex field (J is a declaration; a second square root of -I exists in the kernel instance and the census exhibits many more); the identification of the pair model CMat with Mathlib complex matrices (no anchor shows CMat is an associative ring or equals Matrix m n Complex); the block-ordering convention (all real coordinates before all imaginary ones) is part of the definition: the interleaved ordering gives a different J and a different matrix; states sigma = R(rho)/2, positivity as a theorem (native instances only), effects, instruments / Kraus intertwining (Theorem 3), the balanced tensor lift, or any operational or physical reading; infinite dimensions; the claim that every real channel is a realified complex one (it is not).
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: Complex matrices here are the declared pair model (P, Q) with the hand-written product. R(A) = [[P,-Q],[Q,P]] is an injective ring-linear multiplicative embedding of these into real matrices with J_m R(A) = R(A) J_n and Tr R(A) = 2 Re Tr A, and its image is exactly the real matrices that intertwine the DECLARED J (block coordinate order); the same J^2 = -1 identity holds for other matrices (kernel instance, bounded census), so the choice of J remains an input.
claim_boundary.next_test: Prove in the kernel that R preserves and reflects positivity for Hermitian A, i.e. A is positive semidefinite iff the real quadratic form of R(A) is nonnegative, and that sigma = R(rho)/2 has real trace 1 exactly when Tr rho = 1; the native psd rows are the instances to match.

second_review.notes: Cold read of run 20261021T132245Z_staged. 'ring-linear' is alpha-linearity (R_smul), not complex linearity, correctly. commutes_conj is a general transport statement. Earlier-pass amendments: all applied. The 'many square roots / only +-J commute' sentence now separates the kernel instance from the bounded census (and says the census is not a theorem); does_not_support names the CMat vs Mathlib complex-matrix identification and the block-ordering convention; narrowest_claim begins 'Complex matrices here are the declared pair model (P,Q) with the hand-written product'; interleaved_ordering_same_J, star_without_transpose_sign and positivity_preserved_asserted mutants exist and are rejected (G3_WITNESS:prod_RA_interleaved, prod_RAstar, psd_complex_psd). The checker builds R as I2 (x) P + J1 (x) Q, computes the real product first, decides image membership from the top blocks independently of the commutation test and demands agreement, recomputes Hermitian/symmetric and trace flags, enumerates the integer 2x2 square roots of -I by brute force, and rejects extra fields; no hard-coded values. NEW FINDING (false clause inside the claim boundary). supports says the interleaved coordinate order 'gives a different matrix that does not commute with the block J_n unless n = 1'. The sealed certificate itself contradicts this: among the prod records with n >= 2, interleaved_commutes_block_J is TRUE for A = 0 (2x2), A = I (3x3) and A = iI (2x2), and for A = I the interleaved matrix is not even different from the block one. It is false for the other 5 of the 8 records with n >= 2 (every non-scalar one). The mutant rationale 'equals the block R only for 1 x 1 matrices' has the same over-generality (the mutant itself uses a specific non-scalar record and is fine). The clause is in the sealed p0 profile and in the p2 scope copy. Other observations. (1) other_square_root_instance / other_root_not_in_image are stated for the literal Fin 2 matrices Jstd = !![0,-1;1,0] and Jother over Int, not for J (Fin 1) Int on Fin 1 + Fin 1; the reindexing Fin 2 ~ Fin 1 + Fin 1 is not proved, and other_root_not_in_image says only that Jstd and Jother do not commute, not literally 'not in the image of R'. The supports sentence is worded 'does not commute with J' (fine); the anchor NAME overstates. (2) The psd rows are decided by exact LDL* elimination applied by the same function to A and to R(A), so agreement of the two verdicts is only as independent as that one routine; supports says 'principal minors and by elimination', the checker uses elimination only. (3) 'Tr R(A) = 2 Re Tr A' is the kernel statement trace_R = 2 Tr P; 'Re' is the pair-model real part, consistent with the declared pair model. (4) The DAG node also asserts 'States are sigma = R(rho)/2'; no anchor covers it and does_not_support says so. next_test (kernel proof that R preserves and reflects positivity for Hermitian A and that sigma = R(rho)/2 has real trace 1 iff Tr rho = 1) is the node's own unpaid obligation. earlier_pass.notes: I recompiled lean4/RealificationJ.lean (Lean 4.35.0, exit 0, all 16 anchors on propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only); p1 construction copies are byte-identical to production. The anchors say what supports claims: R_add, R_smul, R_mul, R_one, R_injective are stated for general Fintype index types m n k with DecidableEq and CommRing alpha; J_sq (J*J = -1), J_R_comm (J_m R(A) = R(A) J_n, rectangular), R_imul, R_star (R(A*) = R(A)^T) with hermitian_iff_symmetric (a genuine iff), trace_R (Tr R(A) = 2 Tr P), image_iff (J_m M = M J_n iff exists unique A with R A = M, so the image is exactly the J-commutant, rectangular too), commutes_conj (general conjugation transport of the commutant), other_square_root_instance and other_root_not_in_image (Int, Fin 2: [[1,-1],[2,-1]] squares to -1, does not commute with Jstd, unimodular conjugate). I found no hidden hypothesis or vacuous conclusion. WEAKNESSES. (1) 'complex matrix' is the hand-defined structure CMat alpha m n (a pair of real matrices with a hand-written product); no anchor identifies CMat Real with Matrix m n Complex, or shows CMat is an associative ring. So 'R is a multiplicative embedding of complex matrices' is a theorem about the declared pair model; the identification with Mathlib's Complex matrices is an unpaid (trivial but unstated) bridge. 'ring-linear' is alpha-linearity of R (R_smul), not complex-linearity, which is correct and matches 'J is declared'. (2) The supports/does_not_support text says 'there are many square roots of -I and only +-J commute with J'. The kernel proves only the existence of ONE other square root with its conjugacy (other_square_root_instance) and the general conjugation transport (commutes_conj); 'many' rests on the native census (26 integer solutions in box 5, which I recomputed) and 'only +-J commute with J' is a census fact in boxes up to 7, not a theorem (it is a two-line argument: the commutant of J in M_2(Z) is {aI+bJ}, whose squares equal -I only at a=0, b=+-1, but this is not in the module). (3) The DAG statement also contains 'States are sigma = R(rho)/2'; no anchor covers it. does_not_support names it, good. (4) The block ordering (all real coordinates before all imaginary) is a convention that is part of the definition (the docstring says so); the interleaved convention gives a different J. This is not in does_not_support. CHECKER. check_candidate.py is independent of the producer: it builds R by the Kronecker form I2 (x) P + J1 (x) Q (the producer places four blocks), computes the real product R(A)R(B) first and compares it with R of the complex product, decides image membership from the top blocks R(U, -V) == M independently of the commutation test and demands the two agree (Theorem 2 on each instance), recomputes Hermitian/symmetric from A and from R(A), the trace identity, and a brute-force census of integer 2x2 square roots of -I in the box with the theorem-level consequence 'commuting == +-J'. Leaves are compared with exact types and canonical rational strings; no tolerance; unexpected extra fields are rejected. Rational entries up to 3x3, rectangular, and odd-dimensional refusal are covered. MUTANTS. Genuine near misses: swapped_block_convention (R of the conjugate, still multiplicative), unrestricted_real_matrix_in_image (diag(1,0,0,0)), conjugation_counted_as_complex_linear (diag(1,-1) anticommutes), any_square_root_of_minus_one_is_J ([[1,-1],[2,-1]]) and j_is_the_only_square_root (total 2 vs the true 26 at box 5), symmetric_real_matrix_is_hermitian_image, odd_dimension_has_a_J. trace_is_twice_complex_trace and rectangular_ok_declared_noncommuting are flipped fields. Missing near misses: (a) interleaved (Kronecker I_n (x) [[a,-b],[b,a]]) ordering read as the same J; (b) R(A*) = R(A) (conjugate transpose confused with transpose without the sign of Q), i.e. 'symmetric R(A) for a non-Hermitian A'; (c) 'Tr R(A) = Tr_C A' read as a complex number (partly the first mutant); (d) 'R preserves positivity' presented without proof (the next_test), e.g. a Hermitian A that is not positive semidefinite whose R(A) is indefinite. next_test (kernel proof that R preserves and reflects positivity and that sigma = R(rho)/2 has real trace 1 iff Tr rho = 1) is this node's own unpaid obligation, distinct from does_not_support (which lists states and positivity as excluded, so next_test is the very item excluded; acceptable as 'the next thing to pay', not independent in subject matter). DAG: status DEFINITION and bottleneck 'Lean for Thm 1/2 not looked for' is now stale: Lean for Theorems 1 and 2 (general finite index, commutative ring) exists. The status is a DEFINITION and cannot be raised; add a caveat. The 'states sigma = R(rho)/2' clause and the selection of J remain unpaid.
